The Constitution of 1956 was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on which date?
The Constituent Assembly adopted the first Constitution on 29 February 1956 (1956 was a leap year).
It came into force on 23 March 1956, later celebrated as Republic Day.
Which Prime Minister played the leading role in framing the Constitution of 1956?
Chaudhry Muhammad Ali was Prime Minister when the Constituent Assembly passed the 1956 Constitution.
He also served as Finance Minister and Secretary General of the government earlier.
On which date did the Constitution of 1956 come into force?
The 1956 Constitution was enforced on 23 March 1956 and Pakistan became an Islamic Republic.
23 March is celebrated as Pakistan Day, which also recalls the 1940 Lahore Resolution.
The Constitution of 1956 was framed by the Constituent Assembly in the name of whom?
The Constitution was adopted in the name of the people of Pakistan, as the preamble says.
The Objective Resolution of 1949 was made its preamble basis.
The Constitution of 1956 received its assent from which office holder?
The Governor General (Iskander Mirza) gave assent to the Constitution passed by the Constituent Assembly. He became the first President on 23 March 1956.
The office of Governor General was replaced by the President.
What name did the Constitution of 1956 give to the country?
The 1956 Constitution declared Pakistan an Islamic Republic, the first in the world.
The 1962 Constitution first dropped the word Islamic from the name.
Which part of the Constitution of 1956 dealt with Fundamental Rights?
Fundamental Rights were placed in Part II of the 1956 Constitution.
The Directive Principles of State Policy came in the following part.
Which form of government was provided by the Constitution of 1956?
The 1956 Constitution set up a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister and cabinet responsible to the National Assembly.
The 1962 Constitution changed this to a presidential system.
According to the Constitution of 1956, who was the Head of State?
The President replaced the Governor General as constitutional Head of State.
Iskander Mirza was the first President of Pakistan.
What was the minimum age to become President under the Constitution of 1956?
The 1956 Constitution required the President to be at least 40 years old and a Muslim.
The 1962 Constitution lowered the minimum age to 35.
What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
It provided a single-house National Assembly of 300 members, equally divided between East and West Pakistan.
Pakistan's first bicameral legislature came with the 1973 Constitution.
Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1956?
The 1956 Constitution created the Supreme Court of Pakistan, replacing the Federal Court that existed since 1948. The source marked Federal Court, which is wrong.
The Federal Shariat Court was created much later, in 1980.
Which languages were made national languages by the Constitution of 1956?
Urdu and Bengali were declared the state languages in the 1956 Constitution, with English used officially for 20 years.
Bengali was recognised after the 1952 Language Movement.
Which type of federal structure did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
It provided a federation of two wings, East and West Pakistan, with federal, provincial and concurrent lists.
Powers were distributed through three lists.
How many Articles and Parts did the Constitution of 1956 contain?
The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles, 13 Parts and 6 Schedules.
For about how long did the Constitution of 1956 remain in force?
It was enforced on 23 March 1956 and abrogated on 7 October 1958, about two and a half years.
It was the shortest-lived of Pakistan's three constitutions.
On which date was the Constitution of 1956 abrogated?
President Iskander Mirza abrogated it on 7 October 1958 and imposed martial law.
Ayub Khan became Chief Martial Law Administrator and removed Mirza on 27 October 1958.
Which body enacted the Constitution of 1956?
The second Constituent Assembly passed it, as the first one had been dissolved in 1954.
Governor General Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the first Constituent Assembly in October 1954.
What was the total strength of the National Assembly under the Constitution of 1956?
It had 300 members, 150 from each wing, plus 10 seats reserved for women, so 310. The Constitution also kept parity between the wings.
Today the National Assembly has 336 seats.
How were members of the National Assembly elected under the Constitution of 1956?
The Constitution provided direct elections to the National Assembly, though no general election was held before it was abrogated.
The first direct adult-franchise general election was held in 1970.
What type of citizenship did the Constitution of 1956 provide?
Pakistan had a single citizenship for all citizens, as in a federation like India but unlike the USA.
The 1973 Constitution also has a single citizenship.
Under the Constitution of 1956, how were powers divided in the federation?
Powers were shared through a Federal List, a Provincial List and a Concurrent List.
The 1962 Constitution had only Central and Provincial subjects.
Under the Constitution of 1956, to whom was the Cabinet collectively responsible?
In the parliamentary system the Cabinet led by the Prime Minister was answerable to the National Assembly.
The Prime Minister was the head of government.
On which date was the Constitution of 1962 enforced?
President Ayub Khan promulgated it on 1 March 1962 and it came into force on 8 June 1962. Note the source gave 28 February, which is not the correct date.
Martial law was lifted when it came into force.
In how many Parts was the Constitution of 1962 divided (it had 250 Articles)?
The 1962 Constitution had 250 Articles, 12 Parts and 3 Schedules.
The 1956 Constitution had 234 Articles and 13 Parts.
Which form of government did the Constitution of 1962 provide?
It created a strong presidential system with the President as Chief Executive.
There was no Prime Minister in the 1962 Constitution as originally framed.
How was the President elected under the Constitution of 1962?
The President was elected indirectly by an electoral college of Basic Democrats.
Ayub Khan won the 1965 election against Fatima Jinnah this way.
The electoral college under the Constitution of 1962 was originally formed of how many Basic Democrats?
Originally 80,000 Basic Democrats (40,000 per wing) formed the electoral college.
It was later raised to 120,000 before the 1965 election.
What was the voting age under the Constitution of 1962?
The 1962 Constitution set the minimum voting age at 21 years.
The voting age was lowered to 18 in 1973 and is now 18.
What was the minimum age for a person to be elected President under the Constitution of 1962?
The 1962 Constitution required the President to be at least 35 years of age and a Muslim.
Under the 1956 Constitution it was 40 years.
Under the Constitution of 1962, who had the power to dissolve the National Assembly?
The President held the power to dissolve the Assembly, one of his wide powers. The source asked the Article number, which could not be verified.
Under the 1973 Constitution this power is in Article 58.
Under the Constitution of 1962, who could be impeached by the National Assembly?
The Constitution provided a process for impeaching the President, though it was very difficult to use.
In the 1973 Constitution the President is removed under Article 47.
The Constitution of 1962 provided a federation of the centre and how many provinces?
The federation consisted of two provinces, East Pakistan and West Pakistan.
West Pakistan was a single province created through One Unit in 1955.
What was the original name of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
The 1962 Constitution dropped the word Islamic and called the country the Republic of Pakistan.
The word Islamic was restored by an amendment.
In which month of 1963 did the National Assembly pass the amendment restoring the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
The first Amendment Act was passed in December 1963 and restored the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
The amendment was formally assented in January 1964.
Who was the Chief Executive of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
The President was both head of state and chief executive.
Ayub Khan was the first President under this Constitution.
What was the term of office of the President under the Constitution of 1962?
The President held office for five years.
The 1973 Constitution also gives a five-year term.
Which was the highest court of the country under the Constitution of 1962?
The Supreme Court remained the apex court of the country.
The Supreme Court was first created by the 1956 Constitution.
What type of legislature did the Constitution of 1962 provide?
It provided a single-house National Assembly.
The Senate came only with the 1973 Constitution.
Up to which age could a Supreme Court judge serve under the Constitution of 1962?
The 1962 Constitution set retirement of Supreme Court judges at 65 years.
Under the 1973 Constitution it is also 65 years.
Which languages were national languages under the Constitution of 1962?
Urdu and Bengali were national languages, while English remained in official use.
Which system of local government did Ayub Khan make the base of the Constitution of 1962?
The Basic Democracies system of 1959 created union councils whose members formed the electoral college.
The Devolution Plan was introduced later, in 2001.
Which city was named as the capital of Pakistan in the Constitution of 1962?
The 1962 Constitution named the newly built city of Islamabad as the capital, with Rawalpindi serving as the interim capital while it was being built.
Ayub Khan chose the site of Islamabad near General Headquarters at Rawalpindi.
Under which Article of the 1962 Constitution could the President promulgate Ordinances when the National Assembly was not in session?
Article 29 of the 1962 Constitution allowed the President to make an Ordinance with the same force as an Act when the Assembly was dissolved or not in session and immediate legislation was needed.
Such an Ordinance covered only matters within the competence of the Central Legislature.
Under Article 226 of the 1962 Constitution, who was treated as the first President of Pakistan under that Constitution?
Article 226 (transitional provisions) provided that, following the referendum of February 1960, Field Marshal Muhammad Ayub Khan was to be the first President under the 1962 Constitution.
The 1962 Constitution came into force on 8 June 1962.
Which Order, issued by General Yahya Khan on 30 March 1970, set the framework for the first general elections and for making a new constitution?
The Legal Framework Order of 30 March 1970 laid down the basis for the December 1970 elections and required the elected Assembly to frame a constitution within 120 days.
The LFO also ended the One Unit scheme of West Pakistan on 1 July 1970.
In which month and year was the Constitution of 1962 abrogated?
General Yahya Khan imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.
The 1962 Constitution had come into force on 8 June 1962.
For approximately how many years did the Constitution of 1962 remain in force?
It was in force from 8 June 1962 until 25 March 1969, which is about seven years (nearly six years and nine months).
Which system of government was introduced by the Constitution of 1962?
The 1962 Constitution concentrated executive power in the President, who was both head of state and head of government, so critics called it a one-man show.
The President was elected indirectly by Electoral College of Basic Democrats.
General Agha Muhammad Yahya Khan took over from Ayub Khan and abrogated the 1962 Constitution on 25 March 1969.
Yahya Khan became President and Chief Martial Law Administrator.
On which date was the Constitution of 1973 authenticated by the President of Pakistan?
The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973 and President Fazal Elahi Chaudhry authenticated it on 12 April 1973.
The President who authenticated it was Fazal Elahi Chaudhry.
On which date did the Constitution of 1973 come into force?
The Constitution was enforced on 14 August 1973, the Independence Day, after being authenticated on 12 April 1973.
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became Prime Minister under it.
How many Articles does the Constitution of 1973 contain?
The Constitution of 1973 has 280 Articles divided into 12 Parts.
Articles added by amendments carry letters, for example Article 140A and Article 10A.
On which date was the Objectives Resolution passed by the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
The Objectives Resolution was passed on 12 March 1949, moved by Liaquat Ali Khan.
It became the Preamble of the 1973 Constitution.
According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to whom?
The Objectives Resolution states that sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone.
It adds that the authority is delegated to the State through its people as a sacred trust.
According to the Objectives Resolution, the authority exercised by the people of Pakistan within limits set by Allah is a what?
The Resolution says the authority to be exercised by the people within the limits prescribed by Allah is a sacred trust.
The Resolution says the State shall exercise its powers through the chosen representatives of the people.
According to the Objectives Resolution, through whom shall the State exercise its powers and authority?
The chosen representatives of the people
The Objectives Resolution says the State shall exercise its powers and authority through the chosen representatives of the people.
It also promises democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice as enunciated by Islam.
According to the Objectives Resolution, how shall Muslims be enabled to order their lives?
In accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam

The Resolution says Muslims shall be enabled to order their lives in the individual and collective spheres in accordance with the teachings and requirements of Islam as set out in the Quran and Sunnah.
The Resolution was moved in the Constituent Assembly by Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan.
According to the Objectives Resolution, what freedom shall be given to minorities?
To profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures freely
To follow only the teachings of Islam
To live as decided by government policy
The Resolution says adequate provision shall be made for minorities freely to profess and practise their religions and develop their cultures.
It also promises to safeguard the legitimate interests of minorities and backward classes.
According to the Objectives Resolution, the independence of the judiciary shall be what?
The Resolution states that the independence of the judiciary shall be fully secured.
It also says fundamental rights, including equality of status and opportunity, shall be guaranteed.
According to the Objectives Resolution, Pakistan will make its full contribution towards what?
International peace and progress and the happiness of humanity
The Resolution says the people of Pakistan should attain their rightful place among nations and make their full contribution towards international peace and progress and the happiness of humanity.
This is the closing aim stated in the Resolution and in the Preamble.
In what form was the Objectives Resolution placed in the Constitution of 1973 as originally enacted?
In the original 1973 Constitution the Objectives Resolution was the Preamble. It became a substantive part later through Article 2A.
Article 2A was inserted by the Eighth Amendment in 1985.
What name does Article 1 of the Constitution of 1973 give to Pakistan?
Article 1(1) says Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
The name Islamic Republic was first used in the 1956 Constitution.
After the 25th Amendment of 2018, what do the territories of Pakistan under Article 1 comprise?
Four provinces, FATA and the Federal Capital
The provinces of Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh, and the Islamabad Capital Territory (plus such other territories as may be included)
Four provinces, Azad Kashmir and Islamabad only

The 25th Amendment (2018) merged FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and removed it from Article 1, so Article 1(2) now lists four provinces and the Islamabad Capital Territory. The older answer with FATA is outdated.
Article 1(2)(c) also covers such States and territories as are or may be included in Pakistan.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is Islam declared the State religion of Pakistan?
Article 2 states that Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.
Article 2A makes the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution makes the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution?
Article 2A states that the principles and provisions of the Objectives Resolution (Annex) are made substantive part of the Constitution and have effect accordingly.
It was inserted in 1985 through the Eighth Amendment.
Under Article 5(1) of the Constitution of 1973, loyalty to whom is the basic duty of every citizen?
Article 5(1) says loyalty to the State is the basic duty of every citizen.
Article 5 is in Part I of the Constitution.
Article 5(2) of the Constitution of 1973 describes obedience to the Constitution and law as the what of every citizen?
Article 5(2) says obedience to the Constitution and law is the inviolable obligation of every citizen wherever he may be and of every other person within Pakistan.
Article 5(1) makes loyalty to the State the basic duty of every citizen.
A person who abrogates, subverts, suspends or holds in abeyance the Constitution by force or unconstitutional means is guilty of what under Article 6?
Article 6(1) says any person who abrogates or subverts the Constitution by use of force or show of force or other unconstitutional means is guilty of high treason.
The words 'suspends or holds in abeyance' were added by the 18th Amendment in 2010.
Under Article 6(3) of the Constitution, who is empowered to provide the punishment for persons found guilty of high treason?
Article 6(3) says the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) shall by law provide for the punishment of persons found guilty of high treason.
The High Treason (Punishment) Act 1973 was passed under this Article.
In which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the State defined for the purposes of Fundamental Rights?
Article 7 defines the State as the Federal Government, Parliament, a Provincial Government, a Provincial Assembly and local authorities.
Article 8 follows and deals with laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.
Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution contain the Principles of Policy?
Chapter 2 of Part II, Articles 29 to 40, sets out the Principles of Policy.
Principles of Policy are not enforceable in court, unlike the Fundamental Rights.
Under Article 8 of the 1973 Constitution, a law that is inconsistent with the Fundamental Rights is what?
Void to the extent of the inconsistency
Article 8 says any law inconsistent with or in derogation of the Fundamental Rights shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.
Article 8 itself falls in Chapter 1 of Part II.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law?
Article 9 (security of person) says no person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law.
The Supreme Court has read the right to life broadly to include a healthy environment.
Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution deal with the Fundamental Rights?
Chapter 1 of Part II, Articles 8 to 28, contains the Fundamental Rights.
Articles 29 to 40 contain the Principles of Policy.
What is Chapter 1 of Part II of the 1973 Constitution (Articles 8 to 28) called?
Chapter 1 of Part II is titled Fundamental Rights, the rights guaranteed by the Constitution and enforceable in court.
Chapter 2 of Part II is titled Principles of Policy.
Safeguards as to arrest and detention are provided in which Article of the 1973 Constitution?
Article 10 gives safeguards on arrest and detention, including the right to be told the grounds and to appear before a magistrate within 24 hours.
Article 10A adds the right to a fair trial.
Article 10A of the 1973 Constitution deals with which right?
Right to fair trial and due process
Article 10A guarantees the right to fair trial and due process in the determination of civil rights and criminal charges.
Article 25A deals with free and compulsory education.
Through which amendment was the right to fair trial (Article 10A) added to the Fundamental Rights?
Article 10A was inserted by the 18th Amendment of 2010.
The 18th Amendment also inserted Article 19A (right to information) and Article 25A (right to education).
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution are slavery and forced labour prohibited?
Article 11 prohibits slavery, forced labour and the employment of children below fourteen in factories, mines or hazardous work.
Article 11 also forbids trafficking in human beings.
Article 12 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
Article 12 gives protection against retrospective punishment, meaning no one can be punished for an act that was not an offence when it was done.
Article 13 protects against double punishment and self-incrimination.
Article 13 of the 1973 Constitution gives protection against what?
Article 13 says no person shall be punished more than once for the same offence nor be compelled to be a witness against himself.
Article 12 gives protection against retrospective punishment.
Under which provision of the 1973 Constitution is no person to be subjected to torture for extracting evidence?
Article 14(2) says no person shall be subjected to torture for the purpose of extracting evidence.
Article 14(1) says the dignity of man and the privacy of home shall be inviolable.
Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 15 of the 1973 Constitution?
Article 15 guarantees every citizen the right to remain in, enter and move freely throughout Pakistan and settle in any part of it, subject to law.
Freedom of speech is in Article 19.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is freedom of assembly guaranteed?
Article 16 gives every citizen the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of public order.
Which freedom is provided in Article 17 of the 1973 Constitution?

Article 17 gives every citizen the right to form associations or unions and to form or be a member of a political party, subject to restrictions in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of Pakistan.
Which freedom is guaranteed by Article 18 of the 1973 Constitution?
Freedom of trade, business or profession
Article 18 gives every citizen the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation and to conduct any lawful trade or business.
Article 20 covers freedom to profess religion.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution does every citizen have the right of access to information in matters of public importance?
Article 19A, inserted by the 18th Amendment in 2010, gives every citizen the right of access to information in all matters of public importance, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.
Article 19 itself covers freedom of speech.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is there safeguard against taxation for the purposes of any particular religion?
Article 21 says no person shall be compelled to pay any special tax the proceeds of which are to be spent on the propagation or maintenance of any religion other than his own.
Article 20 gives freedom to profess religion and to manage religious institutions.
In which year did the British Parliament pass the Government of India Act that later served as Pakistan's interim constitution?
The Government of India Act 1935 received Royal Assent in August 1935. After independence it was adapted as the interim constitution of both dominions.
It introduced provincial autonomy and proposed an All-India Federation that never came into being.
Which court was set up in Delhi under the Government of India Act 1935?
The Act created the Federal Court of India, which started work in 1937 and was the apex court before independence.
In Pakistan the Federal Court continued as the highest court until the Supreme Court replaced it in 1956.
What important change did the Government of India Act 1935 make in the provinces?
Introduced separate electorates for the first time
The Act ended dyarchy in the provinces and gave elected ministries real control of provincial subjects, called provincial autonomy.
Separate electorates had already been given by the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
Which province was created by separating Sindh from the Bombay Presidency under the arrangements of the 1935 Act?
Sindh became a separate province in 1936
Sindh was separated from Bombay and became a Governor's province on 1 April 1936 under the 1935 Act.
Orissa was created as a province on the same date.
Under which plan was the partition of India announced on 3 June 1947?
Lord Mountbatten announced the partition scheme, known as the 3 June Plan or Mountbatten Plan.
The Indian Independence Act 1947 gave legal form to this plan.
What did the Indian Independence Act 1947 create?
Two independent dominions, India and Pakistan
The Act divided British India into the two dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947.
Each dominion had a Governor General and a Constituent Assembly that also acted as its legislature.
What happened to the British paramountcy over the princely states under the Indian Independence Act 1947?
It was extended for ten years
It passed to the United Nations
The Act ended British paramountcy, leaving states free to accede to either dominion.
Each state was to decide accession on the basis of geography and the wishes of its people.
Who was the temporary chairman of the first session of Pakistan's Constituent Assembly on 10 August 1947?
Jogendra Nath Mandal, a Scheduled Caste leader from Bengal, presided until the Quaid-e-Azam was elected president.
Mandal later served as Pakistan's first Law and Labour Minister.
On which date was Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah elected President of the Constituent Assembly of Pakistan?
The Assembly met at Karachi on 10 August 1947 and elected the Quaid president on 11 August 1947.
His famous address on that day spoke of religious freedom for all citizens.
In which city did the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan hold its first session?
The first session was held in Karachi, then the capital, on 10 August 1947.
Karachi remained the capital until Rawalpindi became temporary capital in the 1960s.
Which law served as the interim constitution of Pakistan from 1947 to 1956?
Government of India Act 1919 as amended
Government of India Act 1935 with adaptations
The 1935 Act, adapted by the Pakistan Provisional Constitution Order 1947, was used until the 1956 Constitution.
Pakistan thus ran its government under a colonial law for about eight and a half years.
Which Prime Minister moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 7 March 1949?
Liaquat Ali Khan, the first Prime Minister, introduced it and it was passed on 12 March 1949.
Allama Shabbir Ahmad Usmani strongly supported it in the debate.
Which scholar-politician made a key speech supporting the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
Allama Shabbir Ahmad Usmani, a leading Deobandi scholar and Assembly member, spoke strongly in its favour.
Hindu members led by Sris Chandra Chattopadhyaya opposed the Resolution.
According to the Objectives Resolution, democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice are to be observed as enunciated by whom?
The Resolution says principles of democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice shall be fully observed as enunciated by Islam.
It also promised adequate provision for minorities to profess and practise their religions.
Which committee was appointed by the Constituent Assembly in March 1949 to recommend the basic principles of the future constitution?
The Basic Principles Committee was set up on 12 March 1949, the day the Objectives Resolution was passed.
Its first chairman was the Prime Minister, Liaquat Ali Khan.
In which year did Liaquat Ali Khan present the first report of the Basic Principles Committee?
The first report was presented on 28 September 1950. It proposed a two-house legislature and the head of state elected for five years.
It was widely criticised, especially in East Bengal, as it did not give fair representation.
What was the main cause of criticism of the 1950 report of the Basic Principles Committee in East Pakistan?
It gave West Pakistan equal seats in both houses, ignoring Bengal's larger population
It made English the national language
East Bengal had a majority of the population but the report offered it far less than its share, raising a major protest.
It was shelved and later replaced by a new draft after the language riots of 1952.
Who presented the second Basic Principles Committee report in December 1952?
Khawaja Nazimuddin, then Prime Minister, presented the revised report on 22 December 1952.
It proposed an upper house with equal seats for both wings, which angered Punjab.
What number of seats did the Bogra Formula of October 1953 propose for the Lower House?
The Formula proposed a Lower House of 300 seats, with East Bengal getting 165, and an Upper House of 50 seats with equal representation of the five units.
It introduced the principle of parity between East and West, later used in the 1956 Constitution.
Which Governor General dissolved the first Constituent Assembly on 24 October 1954?
Ghulam Muhammad dissolved the Assembly, saying it had lost the confidence of the people.
Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan, its President, challenged the dissolution in court.
In the Tamizuddin Khan case 1955, who was the Chief Justice of the Federal Court that upheld the dissolution?
Chief Justice Muhammad Munir gave the majority judgment, using the Doctrine of Necessity.
Justice A. R. Cornelius was the lone dissenting judge.
Which Federal Court judge gave the dissenting opinion in the Tamizuddin Khan case?
Justice A. R. Cornelius dissented and held that the Governor General had no power to dissolve the Assembly.
He later became Chief Justice of Pakistan from 1960 to 1968.
How many members did the second Constituent Assembly of Pakistan have?
The second Constituent Assembly, formed in 1955, had 80 members elected by the provincial assemblies, with equal numbers from East and West.
It framed the 1956 Constitution under Prime Minister Chaudhry Muhammad Ali.
Who was the Prime Minister of Pakistan when the 1956 Constitution was passed?
Chaudhry Muhammad Ali led the government that got the Constitution passed on 29 February 1956.
He is often called the architect of the 1956 Constitution.
Into how many parts was the 1956 Constitution divided?
The 1956 Constitution had 234 articles divided into 13 parts, with 6 schedules.
The 1973 Constitution has 12 parts and 280 articles.
How many schedules did the 1956 Constitution contain?
It had 234 articles, 13 parts and 6 schedules.
The 1973 Constitution has 7 schedules at the end of the text.
Who was sworn in as the first President of Pakistan on 23 March 1956?
Iskander Mirza was the last Governor General and became the first President when the Constitution took effect.
He was ousted by Ayub Khan in October 1958.
What day does Pakistan observe as Republic Day because of the 1956 Constitution?
The 1956 Constitution came into force on 23 March 1956, making Pakistan a republic.
23 March also marks the Lahore Resolution of 1940.
Who was the last Governor General of Pakistan?
The office ended on 23 March 1956 when Iskander Mirza became President.
Before him came Jinnah, Nazimuddin and Ghulam Muhammad.
How many wings of the country had equal seats in the National Assembly under the 1956 Constitution?
Parity between East and West Pakistan
The 1956 Constitution gave parity: 150 general seats each to East and West Pakistan, plus women seats.
Parity was a compromise to remove Bengali fears over being outvoted.
Under the 1956 Constitution the Prime Minister was to be answerable to whom?
The Prime Minister and Cabinet were collectively responsible to the National Assembly under the parliamentary system.
The President had to appoint as Prime Minister the member likely to command a majority.
What was the term of the President under the 1956 Constitution?
The President was elected for five years by the members of the National Assembly and the Provincial Assemblies.
Under the 1962 Constitution the term was also five years.
What was the highest court established by the 1956 Constitution?
The 1956 Constitution created the Supreme Court in place of the Federal Court.
Its first Chief Justice under the 1956 Constitution was Muhammad Munir.
The One Unit scheme merged which provinces into one province of West Pakistan?
Punjab, Sindh, NWFP, Balochistan and states
One Unit merged the western provinces, Punjab, Sindh, NWFP, Balochistan, and the princely states into West Pakistan.
Its aim was parity with East Pakistan.
Who was the first Governor of West Pakistan, appointed in 1955?
Mushtaq Ahmad Gurmani became the first Governor, and Dr Khan Sahib the first Chief Minister.
Which city was the capital of the province of West Pakistan?
Lahore was the provincial capital of West Pakistan from 1955 to 1970.
Who was the first Chief Minister of West Pakistan?
Dr Khan Sahib, brother of Abdul Ghaffar Khan, led the first ministry of West Pakistan in 1955.
He was assassinated in Lahore in 1958.
Who took over power after the abrogation of the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958?
Ayub Khan as Chief Martial Law Administrator
General Ayub Khan was appointed Chief Martial Law Administrator on 7 October 1958 and became President on 27 October 1958.
He ousted Iskander Mirza on 27 October 1958.
Which commission, formed by Ayub Khan in February 1960, drafted the 1962 Constitution?
The commission was headed by Justice Muhammad Shahabuddin and submitted its report in May 1961.
The government amended its proposals heavily.
On which date did the 1962 Constitution come into force?
It was announced on 1 March 1962 and enforced on 8 June 1962, when martial law was lifted.
The National Assembly first met in Rawalpindi in June 1962.
Which person was elected President in the 1960 referendum before the 1962 Constitution?
Ayub Khan sought a vote of confidence from the Basic Democrats in February 1960 and won as President.
This was the first use of the Basic Democracies as an electoral body.
In which year was the Basic Democracies Order promulgated?
The Basic Democracies Order was issued on 26 October 1959.
It set up a five-tier local government system.
How many tiers did the Basic Democracies system have?
The tiers were Union Council or Committee, Tehsil or Thana Council, District Council, Divisional Council and Provincial Development Advisory Council.
Only the lowest tier was directly elected by the people.
Who elected the President under the 1962 Constitution?
The Electoral College consisted of Basic Democrats, 40,000 from each wing at first.
In 1965 the number was raised to 120,000 in total.
In which year was the first presidential election held under the 1962 Constitution, in which Fatima Jinnah challenged Ayub Khan?
The election took place on 2 January 1965 and Ayub Khan won through the Basic Democrats.
Fatima Jinnah was supported by the Combined Opposition Parties.
In the January 1965 presidential election, which symbol did Fatima Jinnah contest with?
Fatima Jinnah's election symbol was the lantern, while Ayub Khan's was the rose.
She was called Madar-e-Millat, Mother of the Nation.
Who succeeded Ayub Khan as President in March 1969?
General Agha Muhammad Yahya Khan took over on 25 March 1969, imposed martial law and abrogated the 1962 Constitution.
Ayub Khan had resigned under pressure from mass protests.
Under the 1962 Constitution, who was to take over as President if the office fell vacant?
The Speaker of the National Assembly was to act as President for up to 90 days until an election.
Ayub Khan's resignation letter ignored this and handed power to the Army chief.
Which Amendment of December 1963 changed the name of the State to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan under the 1962 Constitution?
The First Amendment of 1963 restored the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan and made Fundamental Rights justiciable.
The original 1962 text had called the State the Republic of Pakistan.
The 1962 Constitution set up which two Islamic bodies?
Advisory Council of Islamic Ideology and Islamic Research Institute
Federal Shariat Court and Zakat Council
Shariat Appellate Bench and Ulema Board
These two bodies were established under Part X, the Islamic provisions, to help bring laws in line with Islam.
The Council of Islamic Ideology exists today under the 1973 Constitution.
What did the Legal Framework Order 1970 abolish?
The LFO of 30 March 1970 dissolved One Unit and restored the four provinces on 1 July 1970.
It also introduced one man one vote in place of parity.
How many seats were fixed for the National Assembly under the Legal Framework Order 1970?
The LFO fixed 313 seats in all, 300 general and 13 for women, with seats allocated by population. East Pakistan got 169 and West Pakistan 144.
The Assembly had to frame a constitution within 120 days.
In what number of days did the LFO 1970 require the new National Assembly to frame a constitution?
The Assembly had to frame the constitution within 120 days of its first meeting, failing which it would be dissolved.
The President also had to authenticate it.
On which date were the general elections held under the LFO, the first on the basis of adult franchise?
National Assembly polling took place on 7 December 1970 and provincial polling on 17 December 1970.
The Awami League won 160 of 162 general seats in East Pakistan.
Which law ended martial law in April 1972 and served as the interim constitution until August 1973?
The Interim Constitution was passed on 17 April 1972 and became effective on 21 April 1972, ending martial law.
Zulfikar Ali Bhutto remained President under it.
Which type of government did the Interim Constitution of 1972 introduce?
Presidential, to become parliamentary after the permanent constitution
The Interim Constitution gave a presidential system, with parliamentary rule to follow under the permanent constitution.
The permanent Constitution was adopted on 10 April 1973.
When did the permanent Constitution of 1973 replace the Interim Constitution?
It was adopted on 10 April 1973, authenticated on 12 April, and enforced on 14 August 1973.
Fazal Ilahi Chaudhry became President and Bhutto Prime Minister.
Under which Constitution were the Basic Democrats given the status of the Electoral College for electing the President?
The 1962 Constitution made the Basic Democrats, elected by adult franchise at Union Council level, the electors of the President and Assemblies.
This indirect system was ended by the 1973 Constitution, which restored direct elections.
In which year did the Federal Court of Pakistan decide the Maulvi Tamizuddin Khan case on the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly?
The Federal Court gave its judgment in 1955 (the Federal Court of Pakistan decision of 21 March 1955), upholding Ghulam Muhammad's action on a technical ground.
The judgment is seen as the start of the Doctrine of Necessity in Pakistan.
The Islamic Provisions of the 1973 Constitution (Articles 227 to 231) form which Part?
Part IX of the 1973 Constitution is titled Islamic Provisions and runs from Article 227 to Article 231.
Part X, Emergency Provisions, follows it (Articles 232 to 237).
Part II of the 1973 Constitution, Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy, covers which Articles?
Part II begins with the definition of State in Article 7 and ends with Article 40 on Principles of Policy.
Chapter 1 of Part II (Articles 8 to 28) has Fundamental Rights and Chapter 2 (Articles 29 to 40) has Principles of Policy.
Part I (Introductory) of the 1973 Constitution consists of which Articles?
Part I covers Article 1 (the Republic and its territories) to Article 6 (high treason).
Article 7 on the definition of State opens Part II.
Part VII (The Judicature) of the 1973 Constitution begins with which Article?
Part VII, The Judicature, runs from Article 175 to Article 212 and deals with the courts.
Part VIII, Elections, follows and covers Articles 213 to 226.
Which Part of the 1973 Constitution deals with Elections (Articles 213 to 226)?
Part VIII is titled Elections and begins with the Chief Election Commissioner in Article 213.
Part IX (Islamic Provisions) comes right after it.
The Emergency Provisions of the 1973 Constitution are in which Articles?
Part X, Emergency Provisions, covers Articles 232 to 237.
Article 232 deals with emergency on account of war, external aggression or internal disturbance.
Part XII (Miscellaneous) of the 1973 Constitution covers which Articles?
Part XII, Miscellaneous, starts at Article 240 (services of Pakistan) and ends with the last Article, 280.
Part XI (Articles 238 and 239) deals with amendment of the Constitution.
Which Articles of the 1973 Constitution form Part XI, Amendment of Constitution?
Article 238 allows the Constitution to be amended and Article 239 gives the procedure.
Article 239 requires a two-thirds majority of the total membership of each House for an amendment bill.
Part V of the 1973 Constitution, Relations between Federation and Provinces, covers which Articles?
Part V starts with Article 141 (extent of Federal and Provincial laws) and ends with Article 159.
Part IV on Provinces runs from Article 101 to Article 140A.
Part III (The Federation of Pakistan) of the 1973 Constitution covers which Articles?
Part III begins with the President in Article 41 and includes the Parliament and the Federal Government up to Article 100.
Article 41 declares that there shall be a President who is Head of State.
Part VI of the 1973 Constitution deals with which subject?
Part VI, Articles 160 to 174, covers finance, property, contracts and suits, including the National Finance Commission in Article 160.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the first Article of Part IV (Provinces)?
Part IV, Provinces, begins with Article 101, which provides for the Governor of a Province.
Part IV ends with Article 140A on local government, inserted by the 18th Amendment.
The remuneration and terms of service of judges are given in which Schedule of the 1973 Constitution (Article 205)?
The Fifth Schedule, linked to Article 205, lays down the remuneration and terms and conditions of service of judges.
The Third Schedule contains the forms of oaths of office.
The forms of oaths of office for the President, Prime Minister and others are in which Schedule?
The Third Schedule of the 1973 Constitution contains the oaths of office.
The Fourth Schedule contains the Legislative Lists.
Which Schedule of the 1973 Constitution contains the Legislative Lists?
The Fourth Schedule holds the Federal Legislative List. The Concurrent Legislative List was abolished by the 18th Amendment in 2010.
Before 2010 the Fourth Schedule had a Federal List and a Concurrent List.
The First Schedule of the 1973 Constitution lists laws that are exempted from the operation of which Article?
The First Schedule lists laws exempted from Article 8(1), 8(2), 8(3)(b) and 8(4), such as certain land reform laws.
Article 8 itself makes laws void that are inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.
The electoral college for the election of the President is provided in which Schedule of the 1973 Constitution?
The Second Schedule, read with Article 41(3), lays down the electoral college that elects the President.
The electoral college consists of both Houses of Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies.
With which words does the Preamble of the 1973 Constitution begin?
Whereas sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to Almighty Allah
In the name of Allah, the Most Beneficent, the Most Merciful
Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic
The Preamble opens with Bismillah and then recalls that sovereignty belongs to Almighty Allah alone.
The Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution of 1949.
In the Preamble of the 1973 Constitution, which leader's declaration that Pakistan would be a democratic State based on Islamic principles of social justice is recalled?
The Preamble says the people are faithful to the declaration made by the Founder of Pakistan, Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah.
Allama Iqbal gave the idea of a separate Muslim state in his 1930 Allahabad address.
Which of these principles is named in the Preamble of the 1973 Constitution as to be fully observed as enunciated by Islam?
The Preamble lists democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice as enunciated by Islam.
The Preamble also pledges that the independence of the judiciary shall be fully secured.
According to the Preamble of the 1973 Constitution, the units of the Federation shall be
The Preamble says the territories shall form a Federation wherein the units will be autonomous with such boundaries and limitations on their powers as may be prescribed.
Pakistan is a Federal Republic under Article 1.
On which date was the Constitution of 1973 adopted by the National Assembly?
The National Assembly passed the Constitution on 10 April 1973; it was authenticated on 12 April and enforced on 14 August 1973.
10 April is observed in Pakistan as Constitution Day.
Who became the first President of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution when it came into force on 14 August 1973?
Fazal Elahi Chaudhry took office as President on 14 August 1973, while Zulfikar Ali Bhutto became the first Prime Minister under the new Constitution.
Bhutto had been President of Pakistan until 13 August 1973 under the Interim Constitution.
Which Amendment removed the Federally Administered Tribal Areas from Article 1 of the Constitution by merging them into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The 25th Amendment of May 2018 omitted FATA from Article 1(2) and merged it into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
The same Amendment changed the National Assembly general seats to 266 by removing the 12 FATA seats.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution provides for the elimination of all forms of exploitation?
Article 3 says the State shall ensure elimination of all forms of exploitation and gradual fulfilment of the principle: from each according to his ability, to each according to his work.
Article 4 gives the right of individuals to be dealt with in accordance with law.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution gives every person the inalienable right to be treated in accordance with law?
Article 4, Right of individuals to be dealt with in accordance with law, protects life, liberty, body, reputation and property from unlawful action.
Article 4 applies to every citizen wherever he may be and to every other person within Pakistan.
Which Amendment added Article 6(2A), barring any court from validating an act of abrogation or subversion of the Constitution?
The 18th Amendment of 2010 inserted Article 6(2A) so that no court, including the Supreme Court and High Courts, can validate such an act.
Article 6(1) defines high treason as abrogating or subverting the Constitution by force or unconstitutional means.
In which year was Article 2A, making the Objectives Resolution a substantive part of the Constitution, inserted?
Article 2A was inserted in 1985 by the Revival of the Constitution of 1973 Order and then protected by the 8th Amendment.
Article 2A was added during the rule of General Zia-ul-Haq.
Under which Article must all existing laws be brought in conformity with the Injunctions of Islam as laid down in the Holy Quran and Sunnah?
Article 227(1) requires existing laws to conform to Quran and Sunnah and prohibits making any law repugnant to them.
Article 227 is the first Article of Part IX, Islamic Provisions.
According to Article 228, the Council of Islamic Ideology consists of members who are not less than eight and not more than
Article 228(2) says the Islamic Council has not less than eight and not more than twenty members appointed by the President.
At least one member must be a person who is or has been a Judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution lets the Parliament or a Provincial Assembly refer a question of repugnancy to Islam of a proposed law to the Islamic Council?
Article 229 deals with reference to the Islamic Council for advice on whether a proposed law is repugnant to Islamic injunctions.
The President or a Governor may make such a reference.
The functions of the Council of Islamic Ideology are laid down in which Article?
Article 230 lists the functions, such as advising Parliament and Assemblies and recommending measures to bring laws in line with Islam.
Article 228 deals with the composition of the Council.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with the rules of procedure of the Islamic Council?
Article 231 is the last Article of Part IX and deals with the Islamic Council's rules of procedure.
Part X, Emergency Provisions, begins with Article 232.
The Federal Shariat Court consists of not more than how many Muslim judges including the Chairman (Article 203C)?
Article 203C says the Federal Shariat Court consists of not more than eight Muslim judges, including the Chairman, appointed by the President.
Chapter 3A of Part VII, Articles 203A to 203J, deals with the Federal Shariat Court.
In which year was the Federal Shariat Court established?
The Federal Shariat Court was established in 1980 by a Presidential Order amending the Constitution.
Under which Article does the Federal Shariat Court examine whether a law is repugnant to the Injunctions of Islam?
Article 203D gives the Federal Shariat Court power to examine and decide whether any law is repugnant to the Injunctions of Islam.
The Court cannot examine the Constitution, Muslim personal law or court procedure.
An appeal against a Federal Shariat Court decision goes to which body?
Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court
Article 203F provides for appeals to the Shariat Appellate Bench of the Supreme Court.
The Shariat Appellate Bench has Muslim judges of the Supreme Court plus up to three Ulema judges.
The Federal Shariat Court is placed in which Part of the 1973 Constitution?
The Federal Shariat Court is in Chapter 3A of Part VII, The Judicature, not in Part IX.
The Council of Islamic Ideology is in Part IX.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution defines the terms Muslim and non-Muslim?
Article 260 contains the definitions, and clause (3) defines Muslim and non-Muslim.
The 2nd Amendment of 1974 added the definition under which Ahmadis are non-Muslims.
Which Amendment of 1974 declared Ahmadis (Qadianis) non-Muslims for the purpose of the Constitution?
The 2nd Amendment, passed on 7 September 1974 under Prime Minister Z. A. Bhutto, added the definition of non-Muslim in Article 260(3).
The 1st Amendment of 1974 dealt with territories after the recognition of Bangladesh.
Islamic way of life is the subject of which Article among the Principles of Policy?
Article 31 says steps shall be taken to enable Muslims to order their lives according to Quran and Sunnah.
Article 31(2) includes compulsory teaching of the Holy Quran and Islamiyat.
Under Article 31(2), the State shall encourage and facilitate the learning of which language?
Article 31(2)(a) and (b) provide for the teaching of Quran and Islamiyat and for promoting the learning of the Arabic language.
Article 251 makes Urdu the national language.
Which Article asks the State to strengthen bonds with the Muslim world and promote international peace?
Article 40 is the last Article of the Principles of Policy and speaks of strengthening bonds with the Muslim world and promoting international peace.
It also asks the State to support the oppressed peoples of the world.
Under which Article may a law be declared void to the extent it is inconsistent with Fundamental Rights, except laws relating to the armed forces or police for discipline, under clause (3)(a)?
Article 8(3)(a) exempts laws about members of the armed forces and police for proper discharge of their duties and maintenance of discipline from the Fundamental Rights rule in Article 8(1) and (2).
This is why Fundamental Rights such as assembly do not fully apply to soldiers in the same way.
In which year was Article 9A, the right to a clean and healthy environment, added to the Constitution?
Article 9A was inserted by the 26th Amendment in October 2024.
The 26th Amendment also changed the deadline in Article 38(f) for eliminating riba to 1 January 2028.
Under Article 10 of the Constitution, an arrested person must be produced before a magistrate within how many hours (excluding travel time)?
Article 10(2) requires production before the nearest magistrate within twenty four hours of arrest, excluding the time of journey.
Article 10(1) gives the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest and to consult a lawyer.
Under Article 10, preventive detention beyond what period needs the approval of a Review Board?
Article 10(4) says no law can authorise preventive detention beyond three months unless the appropriate Review Board has reviewed the case.
Preventive detention laws do not apply to enemy aliens under Article 10(3).
Which Amendment inserted Article 10A, the right to fair trial, in the Constitution?
The 18th Amendment of 2010 added Article 10A (fair trial and due process).
The 18th Amendment also inserted Articles 19A and 25A.
Article 11(3) forbids the employment of children below what age in factories, mines or other hazardous employment?
Article 11(3) says no child below the age of fourteen years shall be engaged in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment.
Article 11(1) abolishes slavery and Article 11(2) prohibits trafficking in human beings.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution declares that the dignity of man and, subject to law, the privacy of home shall be inviolable?
Article 14(1) declares the dignity of man and privacy of home inviolable.
Article 14(2) forbids torture for extracting evidence.
Freedom of speech, expression and the press, subject to reasonable restrictions, is guaranteed by which Article?
Article 19 guarantees freedom of speech and the press, subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of the glory of Islam, security, public order, decency, morality and others.
Article 19A adds the right of access to information.
In which year was Article 19A (right to information) inserted in the Constitution?
Article 19A was inserted by the 18th Amendment of 2010.
Article 19A gives every citizen access to information in all matters of public importance, subject to regulation and reasonable restrictions by law.
The right to profess, practise and propagate religion and to manage religious institutions is given in which Article?
Article 20 gives freedom to profess religion and to manage religious institutions, subject to law, public order and morality.
Article 21 protects against taxation for the purposes of any particular religion.
Which Article safeguards educational institutions in respect of religion, so nobody is forced to receive religious instruction of another religion?
Article 22 says no person attending an educational institution shall be required to receive religious instruction of a religion other than his own.
It also bars compulsory participation in religious ceremonies of another faith.
Which Article gives every citizen the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property in any part of Pakistan?
Article 23, Provision as to property, gives this right subject to the Constitution and reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest.
Article 24 protects property rights from compulsory acquisition except under law.
Which Article protects property rights and bars compulsory acquisition except under a law that provides compensation?
Article 24, Protection of property rights, says no person shall be compulsorily deprived of property save in accordance with law.
Article 24 is one of the rights that can be restricted during an emergency under Article 233.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution declares that all citizens are equal before law and entitled to equal protection of law?
Article 25(1) states equality of citizens, and 25(2) bars discrimination on the basis of sex alone.
Article 25(3) allows special provision for the protection of women and children.
Article 25A provides free and compulsory education for children of which age group?
Article 25A, inserted by the 18th Amendment in 2010, says the State shall provide free and compulsory education to children from five to sixteen years.
Before it, only a Principle of Policy (Article 37) spoke of compulsory education.
Which Article prohibits discrimination in access to public places such as places of entertainment or resort?

Article 26 says there shall be no discrimination in access to places of public entertainment or resort used by the general public, on grounds of race, religion, caste, sex, residence or place of birth.
Article 26(2) allows special provision for women and children.
Which Article safeguards against discrimination in services of Pakistan?
Article 27 says no citizen otherwise qualified shall be discriminated against in appointment in the service of Pakistan on grounds of race, religion, caste, sex, residence or place of birth.
Article 27 is titled Safeguard against discrimination in services.
Which Article is the last of the Fundamental Rights and deals with preservation of language, script and culture?
Article 28 allows any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture to preserve and promote it, subject to law.
Article 29 begins the Principles of Policy.
During a Proclamation of Emergency, which Article lets the President suspend the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
Article 233 gives power to suspend Fundamental Rights during an emergency, and Article 232 covers the emergency itself.
Article 234 deals with failure of constitutional machinery in a Province.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution empowers the President to proclaim an emergency on account of war or external aggression?
Article 232 deals with a Proclamation of Emergency on account of war, external aggression or internal disturbance beyond a Provincial Government's power.
Article 235 deals with a financial emergency.
Under which Article of the Constitution is every organ of State told to act in accordance with the Principles of Policy, with the President reporting on them?
Article 29 says the Principles of Policy are to be observed by organs and authorities of State, and requires an annual report of observance.
Article 29 begins Chapter 2 of Part II.
Which Article states that no action of an organ of State shall be invalid because it breaks a Principle of Policy?
Article 30(2) makes the Principles of Policy non-justiciable, so courts cannot strike down an action only for violating them.
Fundamental Rights, in contrast, are enforceable by courts.
Promotion of local government institutions, with special representation for peasants, workers and women, is covered by which Article?
Article 32 is the Principle of Policy on promotion of local Government institutions.
Article 140A, inserted by the 18th Amendment, requires each Province to establish a local government system.
Which Article discourages parochial, racial, tribal, sectarian and provincial prejudices?
Article 33 says the State shall discourage such prejudices among citizens.
Full participation of women in all spheres of national life is the subject of which Article?
Article 34 says steps shall be taken to ensure full participation of women in all spheres of national life.
Article 25(3) separately allows special provisions for women and children.
Which Article says the State shall protect the marriage, the family, the mother and the child?
Article 35 is the Principle of Policy on the protection of family.
Article 34 is about women in national life.
Which Article of the Principles of Policy safeguards the legitimate rights and interests of minorities, including due representation in services?
Article 36 says the State shall safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of minorities, including their due representation in the Federal and Provincial services.
Article 20 gives every religious denomination freedom to manage its institutions.
Preventing the consumption of alcoholic liquor, except for medicinal and non-Muslim religious purposes, is mentioned under which Article?
Article 37, Promotion of social justice and eradication of social evils, includes preventing consumption of alcoholic liquor.
Article 37 also mentions discouraging prostitution, gambling and obscene literature.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution is titled Promotion of social and economic well-being of the people and refers to social security through compulsory social insurance?
Article 38 deals with social and economic well-being, including social security and reducing the gap between rich and poor.
Article 38(f) says riba shall be eliminated as early as possible.
By what date does Article 38(f), as amended by the 26th Amendment, require the elimination of riba (interest)?
The 26th Amendment of 2024 set 1 January 2028 as the deadline for eliminating riba in Article 38(f).
The Federal Shariat Court had earlier declared interest repugnant to Islam in 2022.
Which Article provides for participation of people from all parts of Pakistan in the Armed Forces?
Article 39, Participation of people in Armed Forces, says steps shall be taken to enable people from all parts of Pakistan to join the Armed Forces.
Article 243 deals with command of the Armed Forces.
How many Articles make up the Principles of Policy (Articles 29 to 40)?
Articles 29 to 40 are twelve Articles, forming Chapter 2 of Part II.
Chapter 1 (Articles 8 to 28) is on Fundamental Rights.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution says that Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan?
Article 1(1) declares Pakistan a Federal Republic called the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
Article 1(2) lists the territories of the Federation.
Articles 203A to 203J of the 1973 Constitution, which deal with the Federal Shariat Court, form which Chapter?
Chapter 3A of Part VII (The Judicature) contains Articles 203A to 203J on the Federal Shariat Court.
Chapter 3A was inserted in 1980 along with the creation of the Court.
Who appoints the members of the Council of Islamic Ideology under Article 228?
The Speaker of the National Assembly
Article 228(2) says the President appoints the members of the Islamic Council.
The Council is based in Islamabad and advises Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies.
Into how many Parts is the 1973 Constitution of Pakistan divided, counting Part I to Part XII?
The 1973 Constitution has twelve Parts, from Part I (Introductory) to Part XII (Miscellaneous).
Article 16 of the Constitution gives every citizen the right to assemble in what manner?
Article 16 gives citizens the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of public order.
Article 17 gives freedom of association, including the right to form political parties.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution makes Urdu the national language of Pakistan?
Article 251(1) says the national language is Urdu and arrangements shall be made for its use as the official language within fifteen years of the commencing day.
Article 251(3) lets a Provincial Assembly prescribe measures for teaching and promoting a provincial language.
Which Article of the Constitution lays down the functions of the Armed Forces to defend Pakistan against external aggression and act in aid of civil power when called upon?

Article 245 says the Armed Forces shall, under the direction of the Federal Government, defend Pakistan against external aggression or threat of war and, subject to law, act in aid of civil power when called upon.
Article 243 deals with command of the Armed Forces.
Which Article of the Constitution deals with the oath of the Armed Forces?
Article 244 is titled Oath of Armed Forces and the form is in the Third Schedule.
Article 42 contains the oath of the President.
Ensuring inexpensive and expeditious justice is a Principle of Policy under which Article?
Article 37(d) says the State shall ensure inexpensive and expeditious justice.
Article 37 is titled Promotion of social justice and eradication of social evils.
Which of these Articles was inserted in the Constitution by the 18th Amendment of 2010?
The 18th Amendment inserted Articles 10A, 19A and 25A among other changes, while Articles 25, 9 and 28 are original.
Article 9A was inserted later by the 26th Amendment of 2024.
The Preamble of the 1973 Constitution ends with the people adopting the Constitution through their representatives in which body?
The Preamble says the people adopt, enact and give themselves this Constitution through their representatives in the National Assembly.
The 1973 Constitution was drafted by a committee of the National Assembly elected in 1970.
The Preamble of the 1973 Constitution says the people of Pakistan shall make their full contribution towards
International peace and progress and happiness of humanity
The Preamble ends with the wish that the people attain their rightful place among nations and contribute to international peace and the happiness of humanity.
This idea is echoed in Article 40 of the Principles of Policy.
Which Article of the Constitution says that the State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges the Fundamental Rights?
Article 8(2) bars the State from making any law that takes away or abridges the rights conferred by Chapter 1 of Part II, and a law doing so is void to that extent.
Article 8(1) makes existing laws void to the extent of inconsistency with those rights.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the office of the President of Pakistan established?
Article 41 says there shall be a President of Pakistan who is the Head of State and represents the unity of the Republic.
The President must be a Muslim of at least 45 years of age and qualified to be elected as a member of the National Assembly.
What is the minimum age to be elected President of Pakistan under Article 41(2)?
Article 41(2) requires a Muslim, qualified to be a National Assembly member, who is not less than 45 years old.
The minimum age for a Prime Minister is the same as for a National Assembly member, that is 25 years.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution contains the oath of office of the President?
Article 42 provides that before entering office the President makes the oath in the form set out in the Third Schedule.
The President takes the oath before the Chief Justice of Pakistan.
Who administers the oath of office to the President of Pakistan?
The Speaker of the National Assembly
Article 42 states that the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of Pakistan, or in his absence by the senior most judge of the Supreme Court.
The Prime Minister takes the oath under Article 91 before the President.
Under which Article can the President grant pardon, reprieve and respite and remit, suspend or commute any sentence?
Article 45 gives the President the power to grant pardon, reprieve and respite, and to remit, suspend or commute a sentence passed by any court, tribunal or authority.
Article 46 deals with the President's right to be kept informed by the Prime Minister.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution can the President be removed or impeached?
Article 47 allows removal of the President for physical or mental incapacity or for violating the Constitution or gross misconduct.
The impeachment resolution must be passed by not less than two thirds of the total membership of the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) in a joint sitting.
What majority of the total membership of Parliament in a joint sitting is needed to impeach the President under Article 47?
Article 47(3) requires a resolution passed by not less than two thirds of the total membership of the Majlis-e-Shoora.
The notice of the impeachment motion must be signed by not less than half of the members of either House.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution lays down that the President shall act on the advice of the Cabinet or the Prime Minister?
Article 48(1) says that in the exercise of his functions the President shall act on and in accordance with the advice of the Cabinet or the Prime Minister.
Article 48(6) allows the President to refer a matter of national importance to a referendum.
Under which Article can the President refer a matter of national importance to a referendum?
Article 48(6) lets the President, after consulting the Prime Minister, direct a referendum on a question of national importance.
The result of the referendum is placed before the Majlis-e-Shoora.
Under Article 49, who acts as President when the office of the President is vacant?
Article 49 provides that the Chairman of the Senate, or in his absence the Speaker of the National Assembly, acts as President.
A new President must be elected within 30 days of the vacancy.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution describes the Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) as consisting of the President and two Houses?
Article 50 states that the Majlis-e-Shoora consists of the President, the National Assembly and the Senate.
The two Houses are the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house).
Under which Article is the National Assembly constituted and its seats distributed?
Article 51 deals with the composition of the National Assembly and the allocation of general, women and non-Muslim seats.
After the 25th Amendment (2018) the National Assembly has 336 seats: 266 general, 60 women and 10 non-Muslim.
How many general seats does Punjab hold in the National Assembly after the 25th Amendment of 2018?
After the merger of FATA the general seats became 266 and Punjab holds 141 of them.
Sindh has 61, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 45, Balochistan 16 and Islamabad 3 general seats.
How many general seats does Sindh hold in the National Assembly after the 25th Amendment?
Under Article 51 as amended in 2018, Sindh has 61 of the 266 general seats.
The 12 FATA seats were abolished by the 25th Amendment, reducing the National Assembly from 342 to 336 members.
What is the normal term of the National Assembly under Article 52?
Article 52 says the National Assembly continues for five years from the day of its first meeting unless sooner dissolved.
The Senate is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved.
What is the quorum of the National Assembly under Article 55?
One half of the total membership
One third of the total membership
One fifth of the total membership
One fourth of the total membership
Article 55 fixes the quorum for a meeting of a House at one fourth of its total membership.
The same quorum rule applies to the Senate.
Under Article 64, after how many consecutive days of absence without leave can a member's seat be declared vacant?
Article 64(1)(b) provides that a member absent for forty consecutive days of a session without leave of the House can have the seat declared vacant.
A member may also resign by writing to the Speaker.
Under which Article can the President dissolve the National Assembly on the advice of the Prime Minister?
Article 58(1) allows dissolution on the advice of the Prime Minister, and the Assembly stands dissolved after 48 hours if the President does not act.
The discretionary power of dissolution in Article 58(2)(b) was inserted by the 8th Amendment (1985) and removed by the 18th Amendment (2010).
Which Amendment first inserted Article 58(2)(b), the President's discretionary power to dissolve the National Assembly?
The 8th Amendment of 1985, passed under General Zia, added Article 58(2)(b).
The 13th Amendment (1997) repealed it, the 17th (2003) restored it and the 18th (2010) removed it for good.
Which Amendment repealed Article 58(2)(b) in 1997 under Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif?
The 13th Amendment (April 1997) removed the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly at discretion.
The 14th Amendment of 1997 introduced the anti-defection Article 63A.
Within how many days must elections be held after the National Assembly is dissolved before its term ends, under Article 224?
Article 224(2) requires a general election within ninety days of the dissolution.
If the Assembly completes its term, elections must be held within 60 days of its expiry (Article 224(1)).
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution lays down the qualifications for membership of Parliament?
Article 62 sets the qualifications, such as citizenship, age, good character and sagacious, honest and righteous conduct.
What is the minimum age to be elected as a member of the Senate under Article 62?
Article 62(1)(b) requires a Senate member to be not less than thirty years of age.
For the National Assembly and Provincial Assemblies the minimum age is 25 years.
What is the minimum age to be elected as a member of the National Assembly?
Article 62(1)(b) requires a National Assembly member to be not less than twenty five years old and enrolled as a voter.
The voting age in Pakistan is 18 years.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution lists the disqualifications for membership of Parliament?
Article 63 lists grounds such as unsound mind, loss of citizenship, conviction for moral turpitude and holding an office of profit.
Article 62(1)(f) requires a member to be sagacious, righteous, non-profligate, honest and ameen.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with disqualification on grounds of defection?
Article 63A was inserted by the 14th Amendment of 1997 to disqualify members who defect from their party.
Article 62 lays down qualifications and Article 63 disqualifications of members.
Which Amendment inserted the anti-defection Article 63A in the Constitution?
The 14th Amendment of 1997 added Article 63A to stop floor crossing by members of political parties.
Article 63A follows Article 63, which lists disqualifications.
How many members does the Senate have today?
After the 25th Amendment (2018) removed the 8 FATA seats, the Senate fell from 104 to 96 members.
Each province has 23 senators and Islamabad has 4.
How many senators represent each province in the Senate after the 25th Amendment?
Each province has 14 general, 4 women, 4 technocrat and 1 non-Muslim seat, that is 23 in all.
What is the term of a member of the Senate?
A senator serves six years and half of the members retire every three years.
Under which Article is the Chairman of the Senate elected?
Article 60 provides that the Senate elects a Chairman and Deputy Chairman from among its members.
Article 53 provides the same for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly.
Under which Article is the Speaker of the National Assembly elected?
Article 53 requires the National Assembly to elect a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker from among its members as soon as possible after the general election.
Article 54 deals with summoning and proroguing the Houses.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution gives the President power to promulgate Ordinances when Parliament is not in session?
Article 89 allows the President to issue an Ordinance when neither the National Assembly nor the Senate is in session and immediate action is needed.
A Governor issues provincial Ordinances under Article 128.
For how long does a Federal Ordinance remain in force under Article 89 unless extended?
Article 89(2) says an Ordinance stops after one hundred and twenty days, and the National Assembly may extend it once for another 120 days.
A provincial Ordinance under Article 128 lasts 90 days.
For how long does a Provincial Ordinance issued by the Governor remain in force under Article 128 unless extended?
Article 128 limits a Governor's Ordinance to ninety days, extendable once by the Provincial Assembly for up to 90 days.
Federal Ordinances last 120 days under Article 89.
Within how many days must the President give assent to a bill passed by Parliament under Article 75?
Article 75 says the President must assent or return the bill with comments within ten days of receiving it.
If he returns it and Parliament passes it again, he has to assent within ten days or it is deemed assented.
Where can a Money Bill be introduced under Article 73 of the 1973 Constitution?
Article 73 states that a Money Bill originates only in the National Assembly.
The Senate can only make recommendations on a Money Bill.
Within how many days must the Senate give its recommendations on a Money Bill sent by the National Assembly?
Article 73(2) gives the Senate fourteen days to make recommendations, which the National Assembly may accept or reject.
The Senate cannot block a Money Bill.
Under which Article is the annual budget statement laid before the National Assembly?
Article 80 requires the Federal Government to lay before the National Assembly the annual statement of estimated receipts and expenditure.
Article 78 creates the Federal Consolidated Fund and the Public Account.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with the executive authority of the Federation being exercised in the name of the President?
Article 90 provides that the executive authority of the Federation is exercised in the name of the President by the Federal Government through the Prime Minister and Federal Ministers.
Article 91 describes the Cabinet and the election of the Prime Minister.
Under which Article is the Prime Minister of Pakistan elected by the National Assembly?
Article 91(4) says the National Assembly elects the Prime Minister by a majority of its total membership.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution limits the size of the Federal Cabinet?
Article 92(1) says the number of Federal Ministers and Ministers of State shall not exceed eleven percent of the total membership of Parliament.
This 11 percent limit was added by the 18th Amendment (2010).
What percentage of the total membership of Parliament may Federal Ministers and Ministers of State form, under Article 92?
Article 92(1) as amended by the 18th Amendment caps the Federal Cabinet at eleven percent of Parliament's total membership.
With 336 plus 96 members, this gives about 47 ministers.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with the vote of no confidence against the Prime Minister?
Article 95 provides for a resolution of no confidence moved in the National Assembly against the Prime Minister.
It must be passed by a majority of the total membership of the National Assembly.
What share of the total membership of the National Assembly must sign a no-confidence resolution against the Prime Minister under Article 95?
Article 95(1) says the resolution is moved by not less than twenty percent of the total membership.
Voting takes place not earlier than three days and not later than seven days after the resolution is moved.
Under which Article does the Attorney-General for Pakistan hold office?
Article 100 provides for the Attorney-General, appointed by the President, who must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.
The Advocate-General of a province is appointed under Article 140.
Under which Article is the Governor of a province appointed?
Article 101 says the President appoints a Governor for each province after consulting the Prime Minister.
A Governor must be a voter, at least 35 years old and a resident of that province.
What is the minimum age to be appointed Governor of a province under Article 101?
