Article 101(2) requires a Governor to be not less than thirty five years of age and a registered voter in the province.
The Governor holds office at the pleasure of the President.
What is the total membership of the Provincial Assembly of Punjab?
The Punjab Assembly has 371 members including women and non-Muslim reserved seats.
Sindh has 168, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 145 and Balochistan 65 members.
What is the total membership of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh?
The Sindh Assembly has 168 members including 130 general, 29 women and 9 non-Muslim seats.
The Balochistan Assembly is the smallest with 65 members.
What is the total membership of the Provincial Assembly of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa after the merger of FATA?
After the 25th Amendment the KP Assembly rose from 124 to 145 members, including seats from the merged districts.
What is the total membership of the Provincial Assembly of Balochistan?
The Balochistan Assembly has 65 members: 51 general, 11 women and 3 non-Muslim.
It is the smallest provincial assembly in Pakistan.
Under which Article is the Chief Minister of a province elected?
Article 130 provides that the Provincial Assembly elects a Chief Minister by a majority of its members.
The Governor appoints the Chief Minister on that basis and administers the oath.
Under which Article can the Governor dissolve the Provincial Assembly on the advice of the Chief Minister?
Article 112 allows dissolution on the Chief Minister's advice, and the Assembly stands dissolved after 48 hours if the Governor does not act.
Article 58 is the matching provision for the National Assembly.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with local government, inserted by the 18th Amendment?
Article 140A requires each province to set up a local government system and devolve political, administrative and financial responsibility to it.
Article 140 deals with the Advocate-General of a province.
Which Amendment of 2010 renamed the North-West Frontier Province as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The 18th Amendment, passed in April 2010, changed the name in Article 1.
It also abolished the Concurrent Legislative List.
The 18th Amendment to the 1973 Constitution was passed in which year?
The 18th Amendment was passed by Parliament in April 2010 under President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gilani.
It changed about 100 Articles of the Constitution.
Which Article extends the Federal and Provincial laws, giving Parliament the power to make laws for whole or any part of Pakistan?
Article 141 says that Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of Pakistan, and a Provincial Assembly for its province.
Article 142 sets out the subjects of law-making.
Under which Article does the federal law prevail when a federal and a provincial law conflict?
Article 143 provides that in case of inconsistency the Act of Parliament prevails and the provincial law is void to the extent of the repugnancy.
Article 144 lets Parliament legislate for provinces with the consent of the Provincial Assemblies.
Which Legislative List was abolished by the 18th Amendment?
The Exclusive List of the Senate
The 18th Amendment removed the Concurrent List from the Fourth Schedule and gave those subjects to the provinces.
The Federal Legislative List now has Part I and Part II, the latter under the Council of Common Interests.
Under which Article is the Council of Common Interests (CCI) established?
Article 153 provides for the Council of Common Interests to be formed by the President.
The Prime Minister is the chairman and the four Chief Ministers are members.
How often must the Council of Common Interests meet according to Article 154?
At least once in six months
Article 154(3), as changed by the 18th Amendment, requires a meeting at least once in ninety days.
The Council is answerable to Parliament.
Who is the chairman of the Council of Common Interests?
Under Article 153 the Prime Minister is the chairman of the CCI.
The Council deals with Part II of the Federal Legislative List and disputes over water and electricity.
Under which Article is the National Economic Council set up?
Article 156 establishes the National Economic Council to review the economic condition of the country and advise the Federal and provincial governments.
The Prime Minister is its chairman.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution protects against interference with water supplies of any province?
Article 155 deals with complaints about interference with water supplies and refers them to the Council of Common Interests.
Article 158 gives priority in natural gas to the province where the well-head is located.
Under which Article does the province where a natural gas well is located have the first priority over its needs?
Article 158 says the province in which a natural gas well-head is situated has precedence over other parts of the country in meeting its requirements.
Article 161 gives provinces the net proceeds of the gas excise duty and hydro-electric profits.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the National Finance Commission (NFC) formed?
Article 160 requires the President to constitute an NFC to recommend how taxes are divided between the Federation and the provinces.
Article 160(3A) says no Award can give a province a smaller share than the previous Award.
At what interval must the National Finance Commission be constituted under Article 160?
Article 160(1) requires the NFC to be constituted within six months of the start of the Constitution and thereafter at intervals not exceeding five years.
In practice the 7th NFC Award of 2010 has lasted much longer.
The 7th NFC Award gave the provinces what share of the divisible pool?
Under the 7th NFC Award (2010) the provinces get 57.5 percent of the divisible pool and the Federation 42.5 percent.
Punjab gets 51.74 percent of the provincial share, Sindh 24.55, KP 14.62 and Balochistan 9.09.
Which province receives the largest share in the 7th NFC Award?
Punjab receives 51.74 percent of the provincial share, based on a multiple criteria formula.
The 7th NFC Award introduced a multiple criteria formula, not only population.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution provides for the Auditor-General of Pakistan?
Article 168 provides that the President appoints the Auditor-General of Pakistan.
The Auditor-General holds office for four years or until the age of 65, whichever is earlier.
What is the term of office of the Auditor-General of Pakistan under Article 168?
Four years or age 65, whichever is earlier
Article 168 fixes four years from the date of assuming office or age sixty five, whichever is earlier.
The Auditor-General can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge.
Under which Article does the Auditor-General submit his audit reports to the President?
Article 171 requires the Auditor-General's reports on Federal accounts to be submitted to the President, who lays them before Parliament.
The Public Accounts Committee of the National Assembly studies these reports.
Under which Article is it laid down that no court has any jurisdiction except what the Constitution or law gives it?
Article 175(2) states that no court shall have any jurisdiction save as is or may be conferred on it by the Constitution or by law.
Article 175(3) provides for separation of the judiciary from the executive.
Which Article provides for the Judicial Commission of Pakistan for appointment of judges, introduced by the 18th Amendment?
Article 175A, inserted by the 18th Amendment in 2010, set up the Judicial Commission and a parliamentary committee for appointing judges.
The 26th Amendment (2024) changed the make-up of the commission again.
Which Amendment altered the judicial appointment process by adding the Parliamentary Committee in Article 175A?
The 19th Amendment (December 2010) changed Article 175A after the Supreme Court's ruling in the Nadeem Ahmad case.
The 18th Amendment first created the Judicial Commission.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the Supreme Court of Pakistan constituted?
Article 176 says the Supreme Court consists of a Chief Justice and as many judges as fixed by Act of Parliament.
Article 177 deals with appointment of judges.
What is the retirement age of a Supreme Court judge under Article 179?
Article 179 says a Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of sixty five.
A High Court judge retires at 62 under Article 195.
What is the retirement age of a High Court judge under Article 195?
Article 195 provides that a High Court judge holds office until the age of sixty two.
The retirement age of a Supreme Court judge is 65.
What is the minimum age to be appointed a judge of a High Court under Article 193?
Article 193(2)(a) requires a High Court judge to be a citizen of at least forty five years of age.
He must also have 10 years as a High Court advocate or 10 years in civil service holding judicial office.
Under which Article is the seat of the Supreme Court of Pakistan fixed at Islamabad?
Article 183 says the permanent seat of the Supreme Court is at Islamabad, and it may sit at other places with the Chief Justice's approval.
The Supreme Court has branch registries in Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar and Quetta.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution allows decisions of the Supreme Court to bind all other courts in Pakistan?
Article 189 says a Supreme Court decision on a question of law, or that enunciates a principle of law, binds all other courts in Pakistan.
Article 188 gives the Supreme Court the power to review its own judgments.
Under which Article must all executive and judicial authorities in Pakistan act in aid of the Supreme Court?
Article 190 states that all executive and judicial authorities throughout Pakistan shall act in aid of the Supreme Court.
Article 191 allows the Supreme Court to make its own rules of procedure.
Which Article gives the Supreme Court the power to review its own judgments?
Article 188 lets the Supreme Court review any judgment pronounced or order made by it, subject to Act of Parliament and rules.
Article 187 allows the Court to issue processes for doing complete justice in any case.
Under which Article does the High Court issue writs such as habeas corpus and mandamus?
Article 199 gives a High Court the power to issue directions in the nature of writs for enforcement of rights and to control the actions of authorities.
Article 203 gives High Courts supervision over subordinate courts.
Which Article gives High Courts supervisory control over the subordinate courts?
Article 203 provides that each High Court supervises and controls all courts subordinate to it.
Article 200 deals with transfer of High Court judges.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with contempt of court?
Article 204 gives the Supreme Court and High Courts the power to punish for contempt.
Article 209 covers the Supreme Judicial Council.
Under which Article is the Supreme Judicial Council constituted?
Article 209 creates the Supreme Judicial Council to inquire into the conduct of judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
It is headed by the Chief Justice of Pakistan.
Who is the chairman of the Supreme Judicial Council?
The senior most High Court Chief Justice
Article 209(2) says the Council consists of the Chief Justice of Pakistan, two next senior Supreme Court judges and two senior Chief Justices of High Courts.
The Council can recommend the removal of a judge for incapacity or misconduct.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution provides for Administrative Courts and Tribunals?
Article 212 allows Parliament or a Provincial Assembly to establish administrative courts or tribunals, with appeal to the Supreme Court.
The Federal Service Tribunal is an example.
Which Chapter of the Constitution establishes the Federal Shariat Court?
Chapter 3A of Part VII, inserted in 1980, set up the Federal Shariat Court under Articles 203A to 203J.
It examines whether a law is repugnant to the injunctions of Islam.
How many Muslim judges does the Federal Shariat Court have under Article 203C?
Article 203C says the Federal Shariat Court consists of not more than eight Muslim judges, including the Chairman.
Not more than three of them are Ulema well versed in Islamic law.
Under which Article is the Chief Election Commissioner appointed?
Article 213 provides for the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner by the President from a list sent by a parliamentary committee.
Article 215 states his term is three years.
What is the term of office of the Chief Election Commissioner under Article 215?
Article 215 provides that the Chief Election Commissioner holds office for three years from the day he enters upon office.
The Chief Election Commissioner must be a retired Supreme Court judge or a person qualified to be one.
Under which Article is the Election Commission of Pakistan established?
Article 218 creates the Election Commission, consisting of the Chief Election Commissioner and four members, one from each province.
Each member is a retired High Court judge.
How many members besides the Chief Election Commissioner does the Election Commission have, one from each province?
Article 218(2) provides for the Chief Election Commissioner as Chairman and four members, each a retired High Court judge from a province.
Members hold office for three years.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution lists the duties of the Election Commission to prepare electoral rolls?
Article 219 states the Commission's duties, including the preparation and revision of electoral rolls and the appointment of election tribunals.
Article 220 requires all executive authorities to help the Commission.
Under which Article can election disputes be decided only by an Election Tribunal?
Article 225 says no election to a House or Provincial Assembly shall be questioned except through an election petition before a tribunal.
Article 226 says elections other than for Prime Minister and Chief Minister are held by secret ballot.
Which Article provides that all existing laws shall be brought in conformity with the Injunctions of Islam?
Article 227 requires all existing laws to be brought in conformity with Islamic Injunctions as laid down in the Quran and Sunnah.
Part IX of the Constitution (Articles 227 to 231) deals with Islamic provisions.
Under which Article is the Council of Islamic Ideology constituted?
Article 228 provides for the Council of Islamic Ideology, with not less than eight and not more than twenty members.
It advises Parliament and the Provincial Assemblies on whether a law conforms to Islam.
What is the maximum number of members of the Council of Islamic Ideology under Article 228?
Article 228(2) says the Council has at least 8 and at most 20 members appointed by the President.
The members serve for three years.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with the emergency due to war or external aggression or internal disturbance?
Article 232 empowers the President to proclaim an emergency if the security of Pakistan is threatened by war, external aggression or internal disturbance.
Article 233 permits suspension of fundamental rights during an emergency.
Under which Article can fundamental rights be suspended during an emergency?
Article 233 lets the President suspend the enforcement of certain fundamental rights while an emergency is in force.
Article 234 deals with a failure of the constitutional machinery in a province.
Which Article provides for the proclamation of emergency in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a province (Governor's rule)?
Article 234 allows the President to take over the executive authority of a province if its government cannot function under the Constitution.
Under which Article can a financial emergency be declared?
Article 235 allows the President to proclaim a financial emergency if the financial stability or credit of Pakistan is threatened.
Article 236 deals with revocation of a Proclamation of Emergency.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution lays down the procedure for amendment of the Constitution?
Article 239 sets the procedure and the two-thirds majority needed in each House.
Article 238 states that the Constitution may be amended by Act of Parliament.
What majority is required in each House for amending the Constitution under Article 239?
Three fourths of the members present
Two thirds of the total membership
Two thirds of the members present
Article 239(2) requires the Bill to be passed by at least two thirds of the total membership of each House.
A change affecting the boundaries of a province also needs two thirds of that Provincial Assembly (Article 239(4)).
Which Article provides that a Constitution Amendment Bill that changes provincial boundaries needs the approval of that Provincial Assembly?
Article 239(4) says that no Bill that affects the limits of a province can be presented for assent without the Provincial Assembly passing a resolution by two thirds.
Article 239(5) says no amendment can be questioned in any court.
Which Amendment of 2018 merged FATA with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The 25th Amendment, passed in May 2018, ended FATA's separate status and merged it into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
It cut the National Assembly from 342 to 336 members and the Senate from 104 to 96.
Which Amendment of 2015 established military courts to try terrorists?
The 21st Amendment (January 2015), passed after the Army Public School attack in Peshawar, allowed military courts to try terrorism cases.
It had a sunset clause of two years, extended by the 23rd Amendment in 2017.
The 17th Amendment to the Constitution was passed in which year?
The 17th Amendment (December 2003) gave constitutional cover to President Musharraf's Legal Framework Order and restored Article 58(2)(b).
It was removed by the 18th Amendment in 2010.
Which Amendment of 2024 introduced constitutional benches and a three-year term for the Chief Justice of Pakistan?
The 26th Amendment was passed in October 2024 and changed Articles 175A, 179 and added Articles 191A and 202A.
Under it a special parliamentary committee picks the Chief Justice from the three most senior judges.
Which Amendment passed in November 2025 created the Federal Constitutional Court?
The 27th Amendment was passed by the Senate on 10 November and by the National Assembly on 13 November 2025.
It also created the post of Chief of Defence Forces by amending Article 243.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution is the command of the Armed Forces defined?
Article 243 provides for the control and command of the Armed Forces, with the supreme command vested in the President.
The 27th Amendment of 2025 rewrote this Article.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution contains the oath of the members of the Armed Forces?
Article 244 requires every member of the Armed Forces to take the oath set out in the Third Schedule.
The oath includes a promise not to engage in any political activities.
Which Article lays down the functions of the Armed Forces, including acting in aid of civil power?
Article 245 says the Armed Forces shall defend Pakistan against external aggression or threat of war and, subject to law, act in aid of civil power when called upon.
Article 245(3) bars High Courts from issuing orders in areas where the Army is deployed.
Which Article provides that Urdu is the national language of Pakistan?
Article 251(1) says the national language is Urdu and arrangements shall be made for its use as the official language within fifteen years.
English may be used for official purposes until arrangements are made to replace it.
Within how many years did Article 251 require Urdu to replace English as the official language?
Article 251(1) set a limit of fifteen years from the commencing day of the Constitution, that is 1973.
Article 251(3) allows provincial languages to be taught and promoted.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution provides for the Federal and Provincial Public Service Commissions?
Article 242 requires the President to set up a Federal Public Service Commission, and each Governor a Provincial Public Service Commission.
Article 240 deals with appointments to the services of Pakistan.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution says that no private organisation capable of functioning as a military organisation can be formed?
Article 256 prohibits private armies and organisations of a military nature.
Article 257 deals with the relationship between Pakistan and the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
Which Article provides that the relationship between Pakistan and the State of Jammu and Kashmir will be decided according to the wishes of its people?
Article 257 says that when the people of Jammu and Kashmir decide to accede to Pakistan, the relationship will be determined in accordance with their wishes.
Which Article defines a Muslim and, after the 2nd Amendment (1974), declared Ahmadis non-Muslims?
Article 260(3) was amended by the 2nd Amendment of September 1974 to define a non-Muslim and include Ahmadis.
The 2nd Amendment was passed under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
Which Amendment of 2012 changed the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and caretaker governments?
The 20th Amendment (February 2012) provided for a caretaker setup and an independent Election Commission.
The 22nd Amendment (2016) changed the qualifications of the Chief Election Commissioner and members.
Which Article was inserted by the 18th Amendment to provide the right to information?
The 18th Amendment inserted Article 19A, giving every citizen the right to access information in all matters of public importance.
Article 10A gives the right to a fair trial and Article 25A the right to education.
In which year was the First Amendment to the 1973 Constitution passed, after the separation of East Pakistan?
The First Amendment was passed in May 1974. It redefined the territories of Pakistan after the loss of East Pakistan and allowed recognition of Bangladesh.
Pakistan formally recognised Bangladesh in February 1974 at the Islamic Summit in Lahore.
In which year was the Second Amendment passed, declaring Ahmadis non-Muslim?
The Second Amendment was passed by Parliament on 7 September 1974 under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
It added clause (3) to Article 260 defining a non-Muslim.
The Fourth Amendment of 1975 is known for providing which new provision?
The removal of the President's power to dissolve the Assembly
Creation of the Federal Shariat Court
Reserved seats for non-Muslims in the provincial assemblies
The Fourth Amendment (1975) provided reserved seats for minorities in the provincial assemblies and also restricted bail powers of High Courts.
Reserved seats for minorities in the National Assembly were already part of the original 1973 text.
Which amendment of 1976 raised the retirement age of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court to 65 and of High Court judges to 62?
The Sixth Amendment (1976) set the retirement ages at 65 for the Supreme Court Chief Justice and 62 for High Court judges.
Under the present Article 179, a Supreme Court judge retires at 65 years of age.
Which amendment of 1977 introduced the provision of a referendum on a vote of confidence in the Prime Minister?
The Seventh Amendment (1977) inserted Article 96 allowing the Prime Minister to seek a referendum on confidence in himself. Bhutto's government was overthrown in July 1977.
The 1977 elections and the PNA movement led to the coup of 5 July 1977.
Which amendment, passed in 1985, gave the President the power to dissolve the National Assembly under Article 58(2)(b)?
The Eighth Amendment (1985) inserted Article 58(2)(b), under which the President could dissolve the Assembly at his discretion.
It also inserted Article 270A, which validated the actions of the martial law period.
Which Article was added by the Eighth Amendment to indemnify and validate the orders of the martial law period of 1977-85?
Article 270A, added by the Eighth Amendment in 1985, affirmed laws and orders made between 5 July 1977 and 30 December 1985.
Article 270A was meant to protect the orders of the martial law period from challenge in court.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution did General Zia ul Haq and later Presidents dissolve the National Assembly before the 13th Amendment?
Article 58(2)(b), added by the Eighth Amendment, was used to dismiss the governments of Junejo (1988), Benazir (1990 and 1996) and Nawaz Sharif (1993).
The 13th Amendment removed it in 1997. The 17th Amendment restored it in 2003 and the 18th removed it permanently in 2010.
Martial law imposed by General Zia ul Haq on 5 July 1977 was lifted in which year?
Martial law ended on 30 December 1985 and the 1973 Constitution was revived with amendments through the Revival of Constitutional Order.
Zia ul Haq held a referendum in December 1984 and non-party elections in February 1985.
Which amendment, passed in 1997 under Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, removed Article 58(2)(b)?
The Thirteenth Amendment, passed in April 1997, removed the President's discretionary power to dissolve the National Assembly and the power to appoint service chiefs.
It transferred the power of appointing the Governors and Chiefs of Staff back to the Prime Minister's advice.
Article 63A, which disqualifies a member who defects from his party, was added by which amendment?
The Fourteenth Amendment (1997) introduced Article 63A on defection from the parliamentary party.
It was passed in July 1997, a few months after the 13th Amendment.
Which amendment, passed in December 2003, restored Article 58(2)(b) and incorporated the Legal Framework Order of Musharraf?
The Seventeenth Amendment (December 2003) gave constitutional cover to the LFO 2002 and restored the President's power to dissolve the Assembly.
It also allowed Musharraf to hold both offices of President and Chief of Army Staff and created the National Security Council.
The Legal Framework Order (LFO) that was later given cover by the Seventeenth Amendment was issued in which year by General Pervez Musharraf?
Musharraf issued the Legal Framework Order in August 2002, before the October 2002 general elections.
The Seventeenth Amendment was passed in December 2003 after an agreement with the MMA.
In which year was the 18th Amendment passed, removing Article 58(2)(b) and giving more autonomy to the provinces?
The National Assembly passed it on 8 April 2010 and President Zardari signed it on 19 April 2010.
The committee which drafted it was headed by Senator Raza Rabbani.
What happened to the Concurrent Legislative List under the 18th Amendment?
It was moved to the Senate only
It was kept but given to the federal government
The 18th Amendment abolished the Concurrent Legislative List, and subjects in it were transferred mainly to the provinces.
Education, health and environment are now provincial subjects, so the Federal List is the only list of the federation.
Which new fundamental right to education for children aged 5 to 16 was added by the 18th Amendment?
Article 25A, added by the 18th Amendment, makes free and compulsory education a right for children of five to sixteen years.
Article 19A (right to information) was also added by the same amendment.
Which Article gave citizens the right to access information in matters of public importance, added in 2010?
Article 19A was inserted by the 18th Amendment (2010).
Article 10A (right to fair trial) was also inserted by the 18th Amendment.
The Judicial Commission of Pakistan for appointing judges was created under which Article by the 18th Amendment?
Article 175A, added in 2010, set up the Judicial Commission and a Parliamentary Committee for appointment of judges.
The 19th Amendment (December 2010) changed its composition after a Supreme Court order.
Which amendment of 2010 revised the composition of the Judicial Commission and the Parliamentary Committee for judicial appointments?
The Nineteenth Amendment (December 2010) reconstituted the Commission and Parliamentary Committee after the Supreme Court sent the 18th Amendment provision back to Parliament.
It also changed the process for appointment of the Election Commissioner.
The Twentieth Amendment of 2012 was related mainly to which subject?
The appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and a caretaker setup
The Twentieth Amendment (February 2012) made the Election Commission independent and defined the process for neutral caretaker governments.
It was passed to guarantee free and fair elections in 2013.
Military courts for terrorism cases were first established through which amendment?
The 21st Amendment (January 2015) was passed after the attack on the Army Public School Peshawar in December 2014, with a sunset period of two years.
It was accompanied by the Pakistan Army Act amendment of 2015.
For how long were military courts first allowed under the Twenty-first Amendment of 2015?
The 21st Amendment included a sunset clause of two years, ending in January 2017.
The 23rd Amendment of March 2017 extended them for another two years.
Which amendment of 2017 revived military courts for a further two years?
The 23rd Amendment extended the military courts' mandate after their term had lapsed in January 2017.
The courts ended in 2019 when the extension lapsed.
Which amendment of 2016 was about the qualifications of the Election Commission members, such as allowing technocrats?
The 22nd Amendment (2016) changed the qualifications of the Chief Election Commissioner and ECP members, allowing technocrats and retired civil servants.
The Election Commission has a Chief Election Commissioner and four members, one from each province.
The Twenty-fourth Amendment of 2017 was passed to fix what issue?
Redistribution of National Assembly seats based on the 2017 census
The 24th Amendment (December 2017) allowed delimitation of constituencies using the provisional results of the 2017 census, in time for the 2018 elections.
The 2017 census was the first since 1998.
In which year was the Twenty-fifth Amendment passed, merging FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The 25th Amendment was passed in May 2018, and the first provincial elections in the merged districts were held in July 2019.
FATA included seven tribal agencies and six Frontier Regions.
After the Twenty-fifth Amendment, how many total seats does the National Assembly have?
Before the merger, the Assembly had 342 seats. After FATA's 12 seats were removed, the number came down to 336, effective from the 2018 elections.
The Senate seats of FATA (8) were also removed, and the Senate had 96 seats after the transition.
Which provision of Pakistan's Constitution was amended by the 25th Amendment to extend the High Court and the Supreme Court jurisdiction to FATA?
Article 247, which governed the administration of tribal areas, was omitted by the 25th Amendment, extending the jurisdiction of the superior courts and of Parliament.
Article 246 defined the Tribal Areas and was also removed.
Through which amendment was the name of NWFP changed to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa?
The change was made in Article 1 by the 18th Amendment in 2010 after the demand of the ANP.
The renaming ended the use of the name North-West Frontier Province, used since 1901.
In which year was the 26th Amendment to the Constitution passed?
The Parliament passed the 26th Amendment in October 2024, changing the way the Chief Justice is appointed.
It was passed when Qazi Faez Isa's term was about to end.
Under the 26th Amendment, the Chief Justice of Pakistan is appointed from how many most senior judges of the Supreme Court?
A special parliamentary committee recommends one name out of the three most senior Supreme Court judges to the Prime Minister, who advises the President.
Justice Yahya Afridi became Chief Justice under this new method in October 2024.
What was the term of the Chief Justice of Pakistan fixed by the 26th Amendment?
The 26th Amendment set a fixed term of three years for the Chief Justice, subject to age 65.
Yahya Afridi was appointed on 26 October 2024.
Which Article of the Constitution, inserted by the 26th Amendment, created constitutional benches in the Supreme Court?
Article 191A provided for Constitutional Benches of the Supreme Court to hear constitutional matters.
A similar bench in each High Court was provided by Article 202A.
In which year was the 27th Amendment to the Constitution passed?
Parliament passed the 27th Amendment in November 2025, and President Zardari signed it on 13 November 2025.
It was passed after the 26th Amendment of October 2024.
Which new court was created by the 27th Amendment?
Constitutional Bench of the Supreme Court
The 27th Amendment created a Federal Constitutional Court to hear constitutional matters and disputes between the federation and provinces.
Justice Aminuddin Khan took oath as its first Chief Justice on 14 November 2025.
Who was the first Chief Justice of the Federal Constitutional Court of Pakistan?
Justice Aminuddin Khan, earlier head of the Supreme Court's constitutional bench, was sworn in on 14 November 2025.
The Federal Constitutional Court was established under the 27th Amendment.
Which new military post was created by the 27th Amendment in Article 243?
Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
The amendment created the post of Chief of Defence Forces, held by the Chief of Army Staff, over the army, navy and air force.
The post of Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee was abolished.
Which post was abolished by the 27th Amendment?
Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee
The 27th Amendment ended the post of CJCSC, whose term expired on 27 November 2025.
The post had been created in 1976 as a coordinating post among the three services.
Under which Article of the 1973 Constitution are the Armed Forces' command and the Chief of Staff appointments provided?
Article 243 deals with the command of the armed forces, and has been amended by the 27th Amendment.
Article 245 deals with the functions of the armed forces, and Article 244 with their oath.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution provides the procedure for amending the Constitution?
Article 238 permits amendment and Article 239 sets the procedure, requiring a two-thirds majority of the total membership of each House.
A bill to amend the Constitution cannot be challenged in any court under Article 239(5).
What majority is needed in each House of Parliament to amend the 1973 Constitution?
Article 239(4) requires a bill to be passed by two-thirds of the total membership of each House.
A bill affecting a province's boundaries also requires the consent of that Provincial Assembly (Article 239(4)).
In which year was the first martial law imposed in Pakistan, abrogating the 1956 Constitution?
President Iskander Mirza abrogated the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958 and appointed General Ayub Khan as Chief Martial Law Administrator.
Ayub Khan removed Mirza after twenty days, on 27 October 1958.
Which President abrogated the 1956 Constitution of Pakistan?
Iskander Mirza announced martial law and the abrogation of the 1956 Constitution on 7 October 1958.
He had become the first President in 1956 under that Constitution.
Which Chief Justice delivered the judgment that validated Iskander Mirza's action in 1958 by using the doctrine of necessity?
In the Dosso case (1958), the Federal Court under Chief Justice Muhammad Munir validated the abrogation based on Kelsen's theory of revolutionary legality.
The Dosso judgment was declared wrong in the Asma Jilani case (1972).
In which year was the second martial law imposed, when Ayub Khan handed over power to the army chief?
General Yahya Khan imposed martial law on 25 March 1969, abrogating the 1962 Constitution.
The Legal Framework Order of March 1970 prepared the first general elections held in December 1970.
Which Supreme Court case of 1972 declared Yahya Khan a usurper and overruled the Dosso case?
In the case of Asma Jilani v. Government of Punjab (1972), the Court held that Yahya Khan's martial law was illegal.
The Court was headed by Chief Justice Hamoodur Rahman.
The Supreme Court validated Zia's coup of 1977 in which case?
In Begum Nusrat Bhutto v. Chief of Army Staff (1977), the Supreme Court used the doctrine of necessity to validate the coup.
Chief Justice Anwarul Haq headed the bench.
What was the name of the military operation by which General Zia ul Haq took power on 5 July 1977?
Operation Fair Play removed Prime Minister Z. A. Bhutto and put the Constitution in abeyance.
Operation Midnight Jackal refers to the 1995 coup plot.
Which instrument was used to put the 1973 Constitution in abeyance after the coup of October 1999?
General Musharraf issued Provisional Constitution Order No. 1 of 1999 on 14 October 1999 and became Chief Executive.
He did not impose martial law formally.
On which date did General Pervez Musharraf take over power by removing Nawaz Sharif?
The coup took place on 12 October 1999 after Nawaz Sharif tried to remove Musharraf as army chief.
Musharraf took the title Chief Executive and not Chief Martial Law Administrator.
Which case of 2000 validated Musharraf's coup and allowed him three years to hold elections?
In Syed Zafar Ali Shah v. Pervez Musharraf (May 2000) the Supreme Court validated the coup on the doctrine of necessity and set a three year limit.
The Court under Chief Justice Irshad Hasan Khan also allowed him to amend the Constitution to a limited extent.
The Revival of Constitutional Order (RCO) of 1985 was issued by which ruler?
Zia issued the Revival of the Constitution of 1973 Order (RCO) in March 1985 to restore the 1973 Constitution with large changes.
The Eighth Amendment later gave the changes constitutional cover.
On which date did President Musharraf proclaim a state of emergency and issue a Provisional Constitution Order, removing the Chief Justice?
On 3 November 2007 Musharraf, as Chief of Army Staff, suspended the Constitution, issued PCO No. 1 of 2007 and removed Chief Justice Iftikhar Chaudhry.
The emergency was lifted on 15 December 2007.
Which Chief Justice of Pakistan was removed by the emergency of 3 November 2007?
He was removed and put under house arrest, and Justice Abdul Hameed Dogar took oath under the PCO.
He had earlier been suspended in March 2007 and was reinstated in July 2007.
Who was the Chief Martial Law Administrator who imposed the first martial law of 1958 and later became President in October 1958?
Ayub Khan was appointed CMLA on 7 October 1958 and became President on 27 October 1958.
He introduced the Constitution of 1962 after martial law was lifted in June 1962.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution defines the act of high treason as abrogating or subverting the Constitution?
Article 6 makes subverting or abrogating the Constitution by force high treason, punishable by death or life imprisonment.
The 18th Amendment added the clause that no court may validate such acts.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution covers a Proclamation of Emergency on grounds of war or internal disturbance?
Article 232 deals with emergency on account of war or internal disturbance. Article 233 deals with suspension of fundamental rights.
Article 234 is about the failure of constitutional machinery in a province and Article 235 about a financial emergency.
Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with the failure of the constitutional machinery in a province, known as Governor's rule?
Article 234 provides for a Proclamation if the government of a province cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution.
Article 235 is the provision for a financial emergency.
In which year was the 1973 Constitution first suspended?
The Constitution was held in abeyance by General Zia ul Haq's coup of 5 July 1977 and was revived in 1985.
It was adopted on 10 April 1973 and enforced from 14 August 1973.
Which Prime Minister was dismissed by President Zia ul Haq under Article 58(2)(b) in May 1988?
President Zia dismissed the Junejo government on 29 May 1988 using Article 58(2)(b).
Zia died in an air crash on 17 August 1988.
How many Articles of the Constitution were changed by the 18th Amendment, roughly?
The 18th Amendment altered, substituted or deleted around 102 Articles, making it the largest amendment.
Parliament's committee had 27 members and it was headed by Raza Rabbani.
Which amendment removed the bar on a person becoming Prime Minister for more than two terms, a restriction added by the 17th Amendment?
The 18th Amendment removed the two-term limit on the Prime Minister and Chief Minister (Article 91 clause 6 and Article 130).
The two-term bar was inserted into the Constitution by Musharraf's LFO.
What is the present number of amendments passed to the 1973 Constitution, after the 27th Amendment of 2025?
Twenty-seven amendments have been made, the latest being the 27th in November 2025.
Not all numbered amendment bills were passed: for example, the 9th and 11th were not enacted.
The Twelfth Amendment of 1991 provided for which special courts?
Special courts for speedy trial of heinous offences
The Twelfth Amendment (1991) inserted Article 212A for speedy trials, for a limited period of three years.
The Nawaz Sharif government passed it.
The Shariat Court of Pakistan was established in which year, by a Presidential Order of Zia ul Haq?
The Federal Shariat Court was established in May 1980 by Presidential Order No. 1 of 1980, adding Chapter 3A to the Constitution.
It examines whether laws are in accordance with the Injunctions of Islam under Article 203D.
